summary:
Aethon is an AI-powered Space Fire Safety research dashboard and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) engine built to decode NASA's microgravity and combustion datasets. Designed for engineers, researchers, and mission planners, it enables users to query decades of NASA microgravity fire research in natural language, validate atmospheric combustion conditions, and quantitatively rank material flammability risks under spacecraft and lunar habitat environments.


Github Repository: https://github.com/GITIHUBB/Aethon
details:
Fire behaves fundamentally differently in microgravity and partial-gravity environments due to the absence of buoyancy-driven convection—changing how flames ignite, spread, and extinguish. Navigating terabytes of dense research across NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository can be overwhelming when designing safe spacecraft or oxygen-enriched lunar habitats.

Aethon solves this by transforming over 40+ technical publications from NASA’s PSI combustion archive into an interactive, searchable intelligence platform. Through a clean web dashboard, users can:

  1. Query NASA Research via RAG: Ask complex engineering and safety questions and receive accurate, source-grounded answers synthesized directly from NASA microgravity experiments (such as SAFFIRE and PSI series studies).
  2. Validate Combustion Physics: Automatically verify whether queried environmental parameters (oxygen concentration, fuel type, pressure) represent physically valid or hazardous combustion conditions.
  3. Rank Material Flammability Risks: Input custom habitat parameters—including oxygen concentration, airflow velocity, ambient pressure, and gravity level to calculate normalized risk scores and rank materials by flammability hazard.

How It Works (Architecture)

  • Data Ingestion Pipeline (ingest.py): Parses NASA PSI research PDFs using pypdf, splits text into overlapping semantic chunks (1,000 characters with a 200-character overlap), generates local vector embeddings via SentenceTransformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), and indexes them inside a local ChromaDB vector store.
  • AI & Inference Backend (main.py): Built with Python FastAPI, featuring asynchronous endpoints (/query-agent and /rank-materials), physics-based condition validation, and a resilient multi-tier AI pipeline powered by Groq (qwen/qwen3.8-27b), OpenRouter automatic failover, and Cohere passage reranking.
  • Interactive Dashboard (microcombust-ui): Built with Next.js (App Router) to provide researchers with an intuitive interface for running literature queries, inspecting safety warnings, and comparing material risk profiles.

Impact & Space-to-Earth Applications

By turning raw microgravity combustion studies into actionable safety insights, Aethon accelerates material screening and fire-suppression system design for long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars—especially in elevated-oxygen lunar habitats where fire risks increase. Additionally, insights surfaced from NASA's microgravity aerosol, smoke detection, and fine-mist suppression experiments directly inform next-generation terrestrial fire safety equipment and smart smoke sensors on Earth.

Tools, Languages & Hardware Used

  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic, Tenacity
  • AI / RAG & Embeddings: ChromaDB, SentenceTransformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), Groq API (qwen/qwen3.8-27b), OpenRouter API, Cohere Rerank, pypdf
  • Frontend: Next.js 14+ (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
  • Data Source: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) Combustion Science Repository (psi.nasa.gov), NTRS - NASA Technical Reports Server (ntrs.nasa.gov)
